Alex — good questions. Short answers up front, then looping in Olga (security) and Rishi (legal) for the technical and contractual detail.

1) Logs: by default our hosted service stores inference metadata and non-sensitive traces for 365 days. Full request payloads may be present if customers do not redact — we recommend application-side redaction for PII. For Private deployments we can enable stricter controls.

2) Encryption: At-rest encryption is always enabled. CMK (customer-managed keys) is currently supported in Private deployments and for Dedicated customers via an enterprise key integration. For Hosted we offer provider-managed keys; we can discuss bringing CMK for larger commitments.

3) RTO: Typical recoveries from incremental snapshots are ~4 hours for Dedicated pools; Hosted restores depend on scope — we typically offer 4–12 hour RTO windows in enterprise agreements.

4) Deletion SLA: Our standard pipeline marks data for deletion and purges active stores within the requested window; backups and immutable snapshots are handled per backup retention policy — we can offer a certified purge flow for Dedicated/Private with confirmation. Attached is a one-page summary of erase/retention options (redwood-erase-sla-options.pdf).

Olga — can you add a short technical note on log types and the backup encryption model? Rishi — can you confirm contractual language options for deletion confirmation?

Ben

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: SOC2 posture + log/backup retention - Medisys discovery follow-up

Alex — hi, Olga from Redwood security here. Added a short technical breakdown below and attached a logs matrix for clarity.

Summary (technical):
- Log categories: 
  * Inference traces (request id, model id, tokens processed, timing) — may include request text unless redacted upstream.
  * Audit logs (user, API key usage, configuration changes) — retained by default 365 days.
  * System logs (compute/infra) — retained per retention policy, mostly used for debugging/SRE.
- KV cache: ephemeral per-session; not persisted across customer sessions in Hosted. For Dedicated/Private we can discuss persistent caching requirements and retention semantics.
- Backups: incremental snapshots captured daily, retained 30 days by default (configurable). Backups are encrypted at rest. CMK support is available for Private deployments and for Dedicated when we integrate with customer KMS.
- Deletion pipeline: data is tombstoned, then expunged during scheduled purge window. For backups we run a separate lifecycle that removes snapshots once retention expires. For customers requiring certified erasure, we can provide a signed confirmation package for Dedicated/Private scopes.

A secure copy of the SOC2 report (full) can be shared via our evidence portal — https://drive.redwood.com/shared/medisys-security-evidence (link above). Please confirm which environments (hosted-prod, dedicated, etc.) are in scope and whether you require CMK.

Attachment: logs-matrix.csv

Thanks, Olga and Ben — that helps. For Medisys the initial compliance ask is: 
- Log retention: 180 days for inference traces + audit logs.
- Backup retention: 90 days.
- Deletion confirmation: written confirmation within 30 days of a purge request covering active stores; certified purge for backups where required (we can define scope).
- CMK: we would like to enable CMK for production if available for Hosted; if not, Dedicated/Private is acceptable.

Next steps: Procurement and Legal want a short SLA addendum and the completed questionnaire. Can you provide a draft SLA (redlined) and confirm timeline for SOC2 evidence access?

Alex Romero
Senior Security PM, Medisys Inc
